user.title: Palo Alto Networks firewall
user.description: Use the management IP or hostname of each firewall (not a dataplane/floating address). For an active/passive pair enter both; leave the second blank for a standalone firewall. The account needs XML API access with Operational Requests.

data_description.secondary_host: Leave empty for a standalone firewall.
data_description.verify_ssl: Recommended. Turn off only if the management interface uses a self-signed certificate or one that doesn't match this address.

reauth_confirm.title: Re-authenticate
reauth_confirm.description: The firewall rejected the stored credentials.

error.same_device: Both addresses point at the same firewall.
error.invalid_cert: {host}'s certificate couldn't be verified (expected with the firewall's default self-signed certificate, or when connecting by IP). Turn off 'Verify TLS certificate' or install a trusted certificate that matches this address.

abort.already_configured: This firewall or pair is already configured.

data_description.update_check_hours: Each check contacts the Palo Alto update server from both firewalls.
data_description.interfaces: Link, speed and throughput sensors are created for these. Only used when automatic selection is off.
data_description.auto_interfaces: On: monitor the WAN-facing interfaces (those used by path monitors and internet routes), following changes on the firewall. Off: monitor exactly the interfaces selected below.

lookup.name: Look up host
lookup.description: Search the active firewall's ARP table and DHCP leases by IP, MAC or hostname. Returns the matching entries.

query.name: Search
query.description: IP address (exact), MAC address (full or partial, any separator), hostname or interface. Leave empty to return everything.

config_entry_id.name: Firewall
config_entry_id.description: Only needed if more than one firewall or pair is configured.

test_security_policy.name: Test security policy
test_security_policy.description: Ask the firewall which security rules a flow hits (CLI 'test security-policy-match'). Without vsys/zones, the flow is traced through every vsys it crosses and tested at each hop; the response lists each hop's rule and an overall verdict.

protocol.name: Protocol
protocol.description: tcp, udp, icmp, or an IP protocol number.

from_zone.name: Source zone
from_zone.description: Source zone. Setting any of vsys or zones tests that single hop; leave all empty to trace every hop.

to_zone.name: Destination zone
to_zone.description: Destination zone. Setting any of vsys or zones tests that single hop; leave all empty to trace every hop.

application.name: Application
application.description: App-ID name, e.g. ssl, web-browsing, dns.

show_all.name: Show all matches
show_all.description: Return every potentially matching rule up to the first allow, not just the first one.

config_entry_id.name: Firewall
config_entry_id.description: Only needed if more than one firewall or pair is configured.

vsys.name: vsys
vsys.description: Virtual system to test in (multi-vsys). Setting any of vsys or zones tests that single hop; leave all empty to trace every hop.

test_nat_policy.name: Test NAT policy
test_nat_policy.description: Ask the firewall which NAT rules a flow hits (CLI 'test nat-policy-match'). Without vsys/zones, the flow is traced through every vsys it crosses and tested at each hop.

protocol.name: Protocol
protocol.description: tcp, udp, icmp, or an IP protocol number.

from_zone.name: Source zone
from_zone.description: Source zone. Setting any of vsys or zones tests that single hop; leave all empty to trace every hop.

to_zone.name: Destination zone
to_zone.description: Destination zone. Setting any of vsys or zones tests that single hop; leave all empty to trace every hop.

to_interface.name: Egress interface
to_interface.description: Egress interface. Leave empty to work it out from the source IP's interface and a route lookup.

vsys.name: vsys
vsys.description: Virtual system to test in (multi-vsys). Setting any of vsys or zones tests that single hop; leave all empty to trace every hop.

config_entry_id.name: Firewall
config_entry_id.description: Only needed if more than one firewall or pair is configured.

route_lookup.name: Route lookup
route_lookup.description: Find the route, egress interface, next hop and zone a destination uses, from the active firewall's forwarding table (Advanced Routing).

logical_router.name: Logical router
logical_router.description: Look up in this logical router only.

source.name: Source IP
source.description: Use the logical router of this source's interface. If neither this nor a logical router is given, all logical routers are searched.

config_entry_id.name: Firewall
config_entry_id.description: Only needed if more than one firewall or pair is configured.

session_lookup.name: Session lookup
session_lookup.description: List live sessions on the active firewall that match the filters (like 'show session all filter'), or show one session in detail by ID.

protocol.name: Protocol
protocol.description: tcp, udp, icmp or an IP protocol number.

application.name: Application
application.description: App-ID name, e.g. ssl or dns-base.

rule.name: Security rule
rule.description: Name of the security rule the session matched.

limit.name: Limit
limit.description: Most sessions to return (the total matching is always reported).

session_id.name: Session ID
session_id.description: Show this one session in full detail instead of searching.

config_entry_id.name: Firewall
config_entry_id.description: Only needed if more than one firewall or pair is configured.

check_for_updates.name: Check for updates
check_for_updates.description: Ask each firewall to check for PAN-OS, content and GlobalProtect client updates and refresh licences now. Returns installed and newest versions when called with a response.

config_entry_id.name: Firewall
config_entry_id.description: Only needed if more than one firewall or pair is configured.

backup_config.name: Back up configuration
backup_config.description: Save each firewall's running configuration as XML in the paloalto_firewall_backups folder of your Home Assistant config, so Home Assistant backups include it. A firewall whose config hasn't changed since its last backup isn't saved again.

config_entry_id.name: Firewall
config_entry_id.description: Only needed if more than one firewall or pair is configured.

keep.name: Keep
keep.description: How many backups to keep per firewall; older ones are deleted.

certificate_expiring.title: Certificate {name} expires in {days} days
certificate_expiring.description: The certificate **{name}** on {firewall} expires on {expires}. Renew or replace it under Device > Certificate Management > Certificates, then commit.

certificate_expired.title: Certificate {name} has expired
certificate_expired.description: The certificate **{name}** on {firewall} expired on {expires} ({days} days ago). Replace it, or delete it if nothing uses it any more (Device > Certificate Management > Certificates), then commit.

licence_expiring.title: {feature} licence on {firewall} expires in {days} days
licence_expiring.description: The **{feature}** licence on {firewall} expires on {expires}. Renew it with Palo Alto Networks, then use Device > Licenses > Retrieve license keys from license server.

licence_expired.title: {feature} licence on {firewall} has expired
licence_expired.description: The **{feature}** licence on {firewall} expired on {expires}. Features that need it stop updating or stop working until it's renewed.

ha_config_unsynced.title: {firewall} config is out of sync with its HA peer
ha_config_unsynced.description: The running configuration on {firewall} has been {state} since {since}. A failover now would run the peer on a different config. Check Dashboard > High Availability, and use Sync to peer from the active firewall if needed.
